UW Grade Distributions: Programs and Class Sizes

Author

Nathan Tesfatsion

Published

October 28, 2026

Loading Libraries

library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)

Loading Data

# Data from reddit user austingwalters in this reddit thread: https://www.reddit.com/r/udub/comments/4e6kxl/i_made_a_website_that_shows_grade_distributions/
# Dataset and FOIA info from their dropbox: https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fo/8lbyazjlt5jmv86jvvs06/AGtgMaWeyZtZuS2fSYLYn_4?dl=0&e=1&rlkey=1sg7t372nhslxogwjl3e9lt9t

uw_grades_original_df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kylethayer/Info-201-au-24-datasets/refs/heads/main/UW-Seattle_20110-20161-Course-Grade-Data_2016-04-06.csv", check.names = FALSE)

# From Course_Number get program abbreviation (Program_Abv) and number (Course_Number_Num)
# From Term get Term_Season
uw_grades_df <- uw_grades_original_df |>
  mutate(
    Program_Abv = str_split_i(Course_Number, " ", 1),
    Course_Number_Num = as.integer(str_extract(Course_Number, "\\d+")),
    Term_Season = str_extract(Term, "Autumn|Spring|Summer|Winter")
  )

Overall Grade Distribution Summary

# number of courses (rows)
num_courses <- nrow(uw_grades_df)

# average GPA and average students
avg_gpa <- round(mean(uw_grades_df$Average_GPA, na.rm = TRUE), 2)
avg_students <- round(mean(uw_grades_df$Student_Count, na.rm = TRUE), 2)

# smallest and biggest course number
min_course_num <- min(uw_grades_df$Course_Number_Num, na.rm = TRUE)
max_course_num <- max(uw_grades_df$Course_Number_Num, na.rm = TRUE)
ggplot(uw_grades_df, aes(x = Average_GPA)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1) +
  labs(title = "Average GPA of All UW Courses", x = "Average GPA", y = "Number of Courses")
ggplot(uw_grades_df, aes(x = Student_Count, y = Average_GPA)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Average GPA vs. Class Size", x = "Number of Students", y = "Average GPA")

There are 39242 courses in the data. The average GPA is 3.41 and the average class has 45.38 students. Course numbers go from 100 to 750. In the histogram most classes are between a 3.0 and 3.9, and the highest bar is around 3.5. Not many classes are below 2.5. In the scatterplot most classes have less than 200 students. Small classes have GPAs all over the place, from about 1.6 to 4.0. Big classes (400+ students) are mostly between 2.6 and 3.8 and almost never get a 4.0.

Comparisons #1: INFO vs. CSE

# get only INFO classes and only CSE classes
info_df <- uw_grades_df |> filter(Program_Abv == "INFO")
cse_df <- uw_grades_df |> filter(Program_Abv == "CSE")

# INFO numbers
info_df |>
  summarize(
    num_courses = n(),
    avg_gpa = round(mean(Average_GPA, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    avg_students = round(mean(Student_Count, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    max_students = max(Student_Count, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
  num_courses avg_gpa avg_students max_students
1         288    3.56        53.01          163
# CSE numbers
cse_df |>
  summarize(
    num_courses = n(),
    avg_gpa = round(mean(Average_GPA, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    avg_students = round(mean(Student_Count, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    max_students = max(Student_Count, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
  num_courses avg_gpa avg_students max_students
1         666    3.43        77.68          673

INFO Graphs

ggplot(info_df, aes(x = Student_Count, y = Average_GPA)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "INFO: Average GPA vs. Class Size", x = "Number of Students", y = "Average GPA")
ggplot(info_df, aes(x = Average_GPA)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1) +
  labs(title = "INFO: Average GPA", x = "Average GPA", y = "Number of Courses")

CSE Graphs

ggplot(cse_df, aes(x = Student_Count, y = Average_GPA)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "CSE: Average GPA vs. Class Size", x = "Number of Students", y = "Average GPA")
ggplot(cse_df, aes(x = Average_GPA)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1) +
  labs(title = "CSE: Average GPA", x = "Average GPA", y = "Number of Courses")

Summary

CSE has 666 classes and INFO has 288. INFO has a higher average GPA (3.56) than CSE (3.43). CSE classes are bigger, with 77.7 students on average compared to 53 for INFO. The biggest CSE class had 673 students but the biggest INFO class only had 163. In the scatterplots, all the INFO classes are under about 170 students and most have a GPA between 3.1 and 4.0. CSE has a lot of really big classes, and those big ones mostly have lower GPAs (around 2.5 to 3.0). The histograms show this too. INFO is bunched up around 3.6, but CSE is more spread out and has a small bump around 2.7. I think the big CSE intro classes are what bring its average down.

Comparisons #2: Small Classes vs. Large Classes

# small = less than 30 students, large = 100 or more students
small_df <- uw_grades_df |> filter(Student_Count < 30)
large_df <- uw_grades_df |> filter(Student_Count >= 100)

# small class numbers
small_df |>
  summarize(
    num_courses = n(),
    avg_gpa = round(mean(Average_GPA, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    avg_students = round(mean(Student_Count, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    max_students = max(Student_Count, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
  num_courses avg_gpa avg_students max_students
1       21254     3.5        20.22           29
# large class numbers
large_df |>
  summarize(
    num_courses = n(),
    avg_gpa = round(mean(Average_GPA, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    avg_students = round(mean(Student_Count, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    max_students = max(Student_Count, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
  num_courses avg_gpa avg_students max_students
1        3122    3.07       196.64          730

Small Class Graphs

ggplot(small_df, aes(x = Course_Number_Num, y = Average_GPA)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Small Classes: Average GPA vs. Course Number", x = "Course Number", y = "Average GPA")
ggplot(small_df, aes(x = Average_GPA)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1) +
  labs(title = "Small Classes: Average GPA", x = "Average GPA", y = "Number of Courses")

Large Class Graphs

ggplot(large_df, aes(x = Course_Number_Num, y = Average_GPA)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "Large Classes: Average GPA vs. Course Number", x = "Course Number", y = "Average GPA")
ggplot(large_df, aes(x = Average_GPA)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1) +
  labs(title = "Large Classes: Average GPA", x = "Average GPA", y = "Number of Courses")

Summary

There are way more small classes (21254) than large classes (3122). Small classes have a higher average GPA (3.5) than large classes (3.07). The average small class has about 20 students and the biggest has 29. The average large class has 197 students and the biggest has 730. In the scatterplots, large classes are mostly 100 to 400 level, and there are barely any above 500. Small classes show up at every level, and the 500+ level ones almost all have a GPA above 3.0. In the histograms, large classes are mostly around 2.9 to 3.0, while small classes are mostly around 3.6 to 3.7. So smaller classes, which are usually higher level, tend to give better grades than big intro classes.
